analysis:
Examined all supplied units and complete changed-range maps. ProviderLoop+Capacity.swift:82 adds serving-authorization supervision to the periodic capacity tick, after several asynchronous maintenance operations. ProviderLoop+Serve.swift head:293,419,429 records initial disconnection, connection transitions and stream termination. The transition call remains in the fast connection-control reader, before authorization clearing and shadow cancellation; slow disconnect cancellation retains FIFO ordering (base:315–321,401–429). No visible change removes authorization invalidation, alters attestation construction or process-key binding, changes encrypted request/response handling, or modifies cache scope, persistence or resource-admission arithmetic. The cache telemetry and T-041 mitigations are unchanged in this file.
Relevant contracts are A-016, TB-011, T-052/T-053/T-057: connection state must not itself grant permission, and supervision must respect grant expiry/revocation without allowing stale queued work. No concrete regression is established by these call-site additions. Integration must examine the unsupplied implementations of noteCoordinatorConnection, event.isConnected and superviseServingAuthorization, including synchronous side effects before clearConnectionAuthorization and interaction with request admission/final writes. Also verify whether supervision's placement after asynchronous maintenance at Capacity.swift:63–81 is compatible with its intended timing contract; this is not evidence that authoritative expiry checks were removed. Existing registration, security-posture collection and encrypted-cache maintenance were inspected as surrounding context, not re-audited. Missing helper implementations leave a material authorization conclusion unresolved.
